questions.prompt: Which resume bullet is strongest for an engineering role?
choices: Redesigned the power regulation circuit, reducing component count by 30% and unit cost by $4
Responsible for designing circuit boards
Worked on circuits with a great team
Helped improve the power system
questions.answer: Redesigned the power regulation circuit, reducing component count by 30% and unit cost by $4
questions.explanation: A strong bullet states what you did, on what, and the measurable result, rather than describing a duty.

questions.prompt: Tailoring an application means choosing which true accomplishments to lead with, not inventing experience the job posting asks for.
questions.explanation: Tailoring is about emphasis; fabricated claims are quickly exposed by technical questions.

questions.prompt: Which items belong in a strong portfolio project write-up?
choices: The problem and its constraints
Design decisions and the trade-offs behind them
What went wrong and how you fixed it
What you would do differently
Only a photo of the finished product
Ten projects described in one sentence each
answers: Design decisions and the trade-offs behind them
What went wrong and how you fixed it
questions.explanation: A portfolio proves your reasoning process; a finished photo or a long thin list does not.

questions.prompt: Put the typical stages of an engineering interview process in order.
questions.explanation: The common pattern moves from a basic fit check through technical depth and behavior to a combined final round.

questions.prompt: Match each part of the STAR method to what it covers.
pairs: The context of the project or circumstance
What happened because of your action
questions.explanation: STAR gives a concrete, evidence-based story structure for behavioral questions.

questions.prompt: In the STAR method, which of the four parts should usually get the most airtime?
questions.explanation: The Action is where your individual judgment and behavior show, so it should be the longest part.

questions.prompt: Which code comment is the most valuable documentation?
choices: Retry count is 3 because the vendor API times out about 1 in 4 calls and 3 attempts clears it 99% of the time
Retry count is 3
Set the retries to three
See code
questions.answer: Retry count is 3 because the vendor API times out about 1 in 4 calls and 3 attempts clears it 99% of the time
questions.explanation: Good documentation explains why, which is the information that disappears once the author moves on.

questions.prompt: Telling a non-engineer "don't worry, it'll just be faster" is good communication because it removes the technical detail.
questions.explanation: Removing the trade-off withholds information the stakeholder needs; good translation keeps decision-relevant facts and drops only the mechanism.

questions.prompt: You found a way to make a feature faster, but it uses more memory. Explain how you would present this to a non-technical product manager.
rubric: Describes the benefit in terms the manager cares about
States the cost or risk plainly
Frames it as a choice or gives a recommendation
questions.model: I would say the feature can respond noticeably faster, but it uses more of the device's memory, which could slow other apps on older phones. I would give a recommendation and let them decide, without explaining how lookup tables work.
questions.explanation: Translate the trade-off into a decision rather than a lecture, and keep the real costs visible.

questions.prompt: Match each response to an identified risk with its meaning.
pairs: Change the plan so the risk cannot occur
Act now to reduce likelihood or impact
Shift the risk to someone else, such as through insurance
questions.explanation: These are the four standard risk responses; each is a deliberate decision recorded in the risk register.

questions.prompt: Why does speeding up a task that is not on the critical path not shorten the project?
choices: The project still waits on the longest chain of dependent tasks
Tasks off the critical path are never needed
Gantt charts ignore those tasks
Those tasks always finish early by definition
questions.answer: The project still waits on the longest chain of dependent tasks
questions.explanation: The critical path sets the earliest finish date, so only changes to it move the deadline.

questions.prompt: When scope, schedule, and budget are all held fixed under pressure, quality is usually what quietly gives.
questions.explanation: Quality is the hidden release valve: corners are cut and testing is skipped without anyone explicitly agreeing.

questions.prompt: Which project is best suited to a waterfall approach?
choices: A permanent bridge whose loads and span are fixed by the site
A new mobile app whose users' needs are unclear
An experimental feature tested on early users
A prototype game with changing rules
questions.answer: A permanent bridge whose loads and span are fixed by the site
questions.explanation: Waterfall fits stable, well-understood requirements where changing physical work mid-project is very costly.

questions.prompt: Which things does every meeting need?
choices: A clear stated purpose
Only the people actually needed for that purpose
A brief written record of decisions and action owners
Everyone tangentially related to the topic
A generic title like "Weekly sync"
answers: Only the people actually needed for that purpose
A brief written record of decisions and action owners
questions.explanation: A meeting needs purpose, the right people, and a written outcome; vague titles and large guest lists make meetings fail.

questions.prompt: You discover that a safety-critical test result was altered before a report went out. Describe what you should do and in what order.
rubric: Raises it first through internal channels such as a supervisor or engineer of record
Names the specific technical risk clearly
Says external reporting is appropriate only if internal channels fail or are compromised
questions.model: I would raise it with my supervisor or the engineer of record and put the concern in writing, clearly stating the safety risk. If that path was ignored or compromised, I would then escalate externally, for example to a regulator or licensing board.
questions.explanation: Whistleblowing is a last resort after internal channels fail, and written documentation protects everyone involved.

questions.prompt: Passing the FE exam earns what title? Give its full name or its abbreviation.
questions.explanation: The FE earns the title Engineer in Training (EIT) or Engineer Intern (EI), not a full license.

questions.prompt: Why is the PE license gated behind several years of supervised experience instead of a single exam?
choices: Engineering judgment is built through supervised real-world practice, which an exam alone cannot verify
The exam is too long to take at graduation
Experience replaces the need for the FE exam
Every engineer must stamp drawings from day one
questions.answer: Engineering judgment is built through supervised real-world practice, which an exam alone cannot verify
questions.explanation: The FE checks knowledge early; the PE plus experience checks the judgment developed over years.

questions.prompt: Match each career path to its description.
pairs: Deep expertise in a narrow technical area
Working competence across many systems and disciplines
Enabling others' technical work through planning and mentoring
questions.explanation: These three common paths are not permanent; many engineers move between them.
